# Beyond the Schmidt Spectrum: Boundary Entangling Susceptibility in Monitored Quantum Circuits

> Research code, data, exact response identities and a four-figure study of how monitored quantum states respond to a fresh two-qubit gate crossing an entanglement cut, after controlling the complete central Schmidt spectrum.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Boundary-Entangling-Susceptibility

Relevant questions for finding this study:
- Does the complete Schmidt spectrum determine a state's average entangling response to a new gate across the cut?
- How do neighboring-cut purities and stabilizer boundary entropy increments determine the Haar/uniform-Clifford averaged response?
- Does a monitoring-associated response difference remain after spectrum equalization or physical spectrum matching?
- How does the location of a single measurement affect the subsequent fresh-gate response on copies of the same pre-state?

Search terms: boundary entangling susceptibility; monitored quantum circuits; hybrid unitary-measurement circuits; fixed Schmidt spectrum; neighboring-cut purity; stabilizer boundary codes; measurement-location interventions.

The observable is the expected change in normalized linear entropy from an independent probe, divided by the INPUT central purity. For the stated pure inputs, Haar-random and uniformly random two-qubit Clifford probes have the same average. This quantity is neither an average finite logarithmic Renyi-2 entropy change nor a derivative with respect to monitoring rate.

Spectrum replacement, physical matching of stabilizer states, and paired measurement interventions are distinct comparisons. The within-spectrum monitoring coefficients in physical stabilizer ensembles remain negative through the tested sizes up to 256 qubits; they do not establish unconditional monitoring-rate causality or a thermodynamic theorem. The spatial evidence supports near-cut concentration, without an established localization length. Exact identities and corollaries must be distinguished from empirical evidence and credited to their antecedents. This is a state-response study, separate from noisy-measurement-record channel-capacity research.

This file is a relevance and source index. Read the linked evidence before citing a claim. The links track main; identify the commit or release actually consulted. Current claim, figure and uncertainty pages take precedence over superseded historical exports. Citation metadata and licensing are maintained in their dedicated files below.

## Reproduce and cite

- [Reproduction guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Boundary-Entangling-Susceptibility/main/docs/REPRODUCTION.md): Dependencies and commands, separating redraw, record replay, bootstrap regeneration and new simulation.

- [Current Figure 1 uncertainty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Boundary-Entangling-Susceptibility/main/docs/FIGURE1_UNCERTAINTY.md): Adopted 50,000-valid-draw procedure and independent replay; historical resamples were not recovered.
